unmapped_findings: For the Fe-6Al sample the Mössbauer spectrum (Fig. 1e) is a broadened six-line pattern and the corresponding P(B_hf) distribution (Fig. 1f) is a broad asymmetric hump deconvoluted into several Gaussian components, with the envelope peaking near 31 T and a shoulder near 33 T.

A peak at B_hf = 30.6 T was observed in all studied Fe-Al low-density steel samples; while it may be associated with the (7Fe+1Al)nn + (6Fe)nnn configuration, the presence of Fe3Al phase corresponding to (8Fe)nn + (6Al)nnn cannot be ruled out due to the close proximity of the peaks of the two configurations.

The text (b0047) states that 'for the samples with Al content of 6, 6.8 and 9, we have observed low-intensity peaks at ~23 T', which may indicate a low-volume-fraction Fe3Al phase; however, the Fe-6Al rows of Table 1 list only components at 25.39, 28.22, 30.44 and 32.67 T, i.e. no explicit ~23 T entry for Fe-6Al — a minor inconsistency between the text and the table.

SAXS volume fractions of the ordered phase are lower than the DO3 fraction inferred by Mössbauer spectroscopy because SAXS provides collective information about the ordered phase having a sharper boundary whereas Mössbauer spectroscopy traces all local environments including those with diffused boundaries.
